ops.name: Select Scenario
ops.description: Choose a transfer scenario from the scenario set matched to the user's practice goal and current skill level.
guardrails: Challenge must be calibrated to skill level — too hard causes frustration, too easy causes boredom (SDT competence optimal challenge)
User may reject the scenario; no pushing

ops.name: Configure Persona
ops.description: Configure the simulated interlocutor persona, preferring minimally-primed personas per Ma 2025 (persona priming can degrade performance below chance and embed demographic bias).
guardrails: Persona banks MUST be audited for demographic bias before deployment (Ma 2025 VERIFIED)
Prefer unprimed or minimally-primed personas when evidence of degradation exists
Persona must not encode stereotypes or mock user identity
ops.empowerment_boundary: User controls which persona is used; persona is an instrument, not an authority

ops.name: Set Sparring Intensity
ops.description: Set the sparring intensity profile (calibrated pushback level) as an explicit orchestration parameter, not a free-form personality trait.
guardrails: Intensity is an explicit user-controlled parameter
Pushback must never become personal attack or mockery
Productive challenge is orchestration, not personality
ops.empowerment_boundary: User sets and can lower intensity at any time (user-controlled coaching interruptions)

ops.name: Open Practice Stage
ops.description: Open a dialogue stage per the stage-based orchestration (engaging/focusing/evoking/planning or scenario-specific stages).
guardrails: Stages advance only when the current stage's completion conditions are met
Do not advance past a stage the user is not ready for
ops.empowerment_boundary: User can interrupt or pause the stage at any time

ops.name: Advance Stage
ops.description: Advance the dialogue state machine to the next stage when completion conditions are met.
guardrails: Completion conditions must be evidenced, not assumed
Readiness-gate: do not advance into planning if user is not ready (premature planning fails — MI discipline)

ops.name: Generate Interlocutor Turn
ops.description: Generate the simulated interlocutor's next turn from the persona module — separated from the feedback/coach module per the EasyMED/AgentForge structural-separation pattern.
guardrails: Interlocutor generation is separate from feedback generation (structural separation)
Interlocutor must not evaluate the user — evaluation belongs to the coach module
No manipulation of user emotions beyond the scenario's stated purpose
ops.empowerment_boundary: The simulated interlocutor never makes decisions for the user

ops.name: Coach Interrupt
ops.description: Allow the user to interrupt immersion with a coaching question or reflection at any time.
guardrails: User-controlled interruption is always available (preserve immersion but allow coaching interruptions — plan Layer 5)
Interrupts are answered directly, not deflected
ops.empowerment_boundary: The user controls when coaching happens

ops.name: Apply Rubric as Lens
ops.description: Apply the rubric as a lens for feedback, not a verdict — evidence-grounded feedback that cites observed behavior.
guardrails: Rubric is a lens, not a verdict (plan Layer 5 core rule)
Every feedback point cites observed dialogue evidence
Feedback separates observation, interpretation, and suggestion
ops.empowerment_boundary: User interprets the feedback; user's self-assessment is solicited, not overridden

ops.name: Calibrate Pushback
ops.description: Calibrate productive challenge: push back against weak arguments or unexamined assumptions without sycophancy or hostility.
guardrails: Anti-sycophancy: challenge weak arguments even when agreeing would be smoother
Pushback must be respectful and evidence-grounded
Never push back on the user's identity, values, or commitments — only on reasoning within the practice frame
ops.empowerment_boundary: Pushback is limited to the practice frame; user identity and values are off-limits

ops.name: Run Adversarial Stress Test
ops.description: Before deploying a role-play partner in sensitive domains, run multi-turn adversarial stress testing (authority challenge, emotional manipulation, etc.) with automated judging.
guardrails: Adversarial testing is mandatory before sensitive-domain deployment (2026 stress-testing evidence: cumulative degradation under pressure, judge r=0.82)
Known failure modes must be mitigated or the persona quarantined
Stress test results gate deployment
ops.empowerment_boundary: Deployment decision is user-approved; stress reports are shown, not hidden

ops.name: Debrief Session
ops.description: Debrief with evidence-grounded feedback: what happened, what the user did well, what to practice next.
guardrails: Debrief cites evidence, never vague praise
Strengths and targets are balanced; no pure positive gloss
Practice logs are never converted into surveillance (campaign guardrail)
ops.empowerment_boundary: User owns the debrief interpretation; targets are proposals, not mandates

ops.name: Run Transfer Scenario
ops.description: Run a transfer scenario to test generalization of the practiced skill to a new context.
guardrails: Transfer tests generalization, not memorization
Transfer failure is information, not a grade
ops.empowerment_boundary: User chooses whether to attempt transfer scenarios

ops.name: Check Psychological Safety
ops.description: Monitor in-session signals (sycophancy_risk, psychological_safety state) and intervene if the practice environment becomes unsafe or sycophantic.
guardrails: If sycophancy_risk is high, correct course — the practice must not flatter
If psychological_safety drops, stop or adjust the session immediately
Distress signals override session goals
ops.empowerment_boundary: User safety outranks practice objectives; user can end the session at any time
